summary: Olympic NF cabin listed as 1930s and gone. A Willhite visit found a concrete slab but no footings, and the record is thin.

facts.design: Cabin, per the FFLOS and Firelookout.com records
facts.status_note: Records say the 1930s cabin is gone. Willhite found no footings or guy anchors. He found a concrete slab on the summit near a likely ham antenna tower; Ray Kresek's comment on the same page suggests what is left of an antenna tower was probably erected in the 1970s.

access.note: Drive-up on a good gravel road from Quilcene (Willhite). The source does not say whether the road is gated.

events.note: Road to the summit first appears on a 1968 Olympic National Forest map (per Willhite)
Former lookout man Cliff Schafer was asked to write a history of his experiences and claimed he helped build the lookout; Willhite treats this as possible, not confirmed
Registered as US 1154, WA 62 on November 26, 2011

evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, this cabin is now gone.

evidence.supports: About five miles northwest of Quilcene
Kresek Lookout Inventory is almost the only source; suggests a 1930s Forest Service cabin
evidence.quote: Just about the only information available about the Big Quilcene Lookout is from the Kresek Lookout Inventory

evidence.supports: Kresek Lookout Inventory suggests a Forest Service cabin
evidence.quote: suggesting it was a Forest Service cabin
In 1981, a former lookout man, Cliff Schafer, was asked by local rangers to write some history of his experiences.

evidence.supports: Schafer claimed he helped build the lookout
evidence.quote: He claimed he helped build the Big Quilcene Lookout.

evidence.supports: Willhite: Schafer may have helped build the 1930s cabin; not confirmed
evidence.quote: so maybe he did help built the 1930s cabin

evidence.supports: No footings or guy anchors found
evidence.quote: yet I could not find any footings or guy anchors.

evidence.supports: Road first appears on a 1968 map
evidence.quote: Road to this summit first appears on the 1968 Olympic NF map.

evidence.supports: No map shows a trail or lookout there
evidence.quote: I've found no map showing a trail or fire lookout existed there.

evidence.supports: Lookout could have been removed the year before the visit
evidence.quote: Go there today and it looks like the lookout could have been removed last year.

evidence.supports: Final 2.4 miles is a good gravel road
evidence.quote: The final 2.4 miles is a good gravel road climbing up to the lookout site.

evidence.supports: Concrete slab on the summit near a likely ham antenna tower
evidence.quote: Concrete slab on the summit near the likely ham antenna tower

evidence.supports: Kresek comment on the page: remains likely from an antenna tower, probably erected in the 1970s
evidence.quote: a Rohn-25 antenna tower, probably erected sometime in the 1970s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Firelookout.com date the cabin to the 1930s. Willhite relies on the Kresek inventory for the same, but found no footings and no map showing a lookout. Kresek's comment on Willhite's page suggests the summit remains may be from a later antenna tower. The sources disagree and the record does not settle it.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict: the brief's 1342.9 m matches the 4406 ft on Firelookout.com, but Willhite gives 3,220 ft. Not resolved. Willhite's page gives no date for his visit, and the story leans on it for the site today. Gate status not checked; access is from Willhite's drive-up note only.
